issues.author: mcwitt
issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This campaign tested whether the ragged EP64 all-to-all path could match the fixed-transport hero throughput target while keeping trained-router drops below 2% at the full 8/384 hero shape on one NVL72 rack. The drop criterion is met with large margin: the real-LR drop-trajectory run averaged 0.107% drops over steps 250-299 at cf 1.15. Throughput improved from the initial 20.20% MFU / 223k tok/s configuration to a 21.82% MFU / 241k tok/s frontier after QuACK GEMM scheduling work, with zero drops and bit-identical loss across the tuning arms. The issue's current conclusion is that the in-scope configuration and compute-tuning levers are exhausted: split counts, store width, symmetric buffers, fused device kernel, command buffers, HBM optimizer residency, GEMM tile/cluster/persistence, backward mask removal, and overlap-limit changes do not close the remaining gap. Reaching the original ~25% / ~300k tok/s target now depends on a faster structural transport path, tracked separately in marin-ep, rather than more launch-flag tuning here.

### Helpful links
- Prior ragged EP64 crash/fix campaign: #8077
- Capacity/drop analysis: #8062
- Upstream ragged all-to-all gate: https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/47283
- Configuration phase conclusion: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8317#issuecomment-5305649465
- Compute-tuning frontier: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8317#issuecomment-5308322722
- Final in-scope lever closure: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8317#issuecomment-5309167198
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## TL;DR

Campaign start. The ragged all-to-all hero (E384, top-8, i3072, EP64 on one NVL72 rack) runs at 20.20% MFU / 223k tokens/s (`ra2a-mw-g17`, cf 1.00, LR≈0 harness). The goal is throughput comparable to the fixed-transport `moe_hero_ep` template (~25% MFU, ~300k tokens/s per rack) while holding steady-state trained-router drops under 2%.

## Description

#8077 root-caused and fixed the EP64 one-shot crash (openxla/xla#47283, kMaxPeers rebuild wheel) and validated the first ragged EP64 hero run. The ragged transport pools receiver capacity per device, so it drops far less than `fixed_all_to_all` at the same capacity factor: at cf 1.1–1.2 the trained-regime drop rate measures ≤0.05% (analytical replay of #8062 histograms; empirical r02 at EP16), versus ~4% for the fixed template at cf 1.30–1.33. What remains is a throughput gap.

Reference points at hero scale on one rack: fixed transport at iso-active-compute (`mhep-baseline-e192k4-i6144-cf133-fp32-20260814-c`) reaches 23.6% MFU / 251k tokens/s at ~3.9% drops; the half-active-compute reference (`mhep-baseline-e192k4-cf133-fp32-20260814-b`, i3072) reaches 25.3% / 346k.

Constraints: no model change, and no quantization beyond what `moe_hero_ep` on main already performs (per the [fidelity discussion](https://openathena.slack.com/archives/C0AHF5KV11Q/p1786740832465729?thread_ts=1786583521.652629&cid=C0AHF5KV11Q)). The ragged training path is currently bf16 end to end.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Reach ~25% MFU / ~300k tokens/s at the full hero shape (d6144/L48, E384, top-8, i3072, latent 3072, batch 1024) on one NVL72 rack with the ragged transport, then demonstrate <2% steady-state drops at the chosen capacity posture and loss parity against the existing EP implementation via `small_scale_abl_launch.py`.

## Status

h01 (cf 1.15 posture baseline) and h02 (latency-hiding scheduler + overlap limit 4, retesting the safe-flag retreat adopted on the broken barrier generation) are running. Queued: splits-per-peer sweep at EP64, command buffers at the #8277 capture set, XProf anatomy of the best configuration.

## Links

* Logbook: `.agents/logbooks/ragged-ep64.md` (branch `ra2a-mw/s48-diag`)
* Prior campaign: #8077
* Upstream fix: https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/47283
* Capacity/drop analysis: #8062
* W&B: runs under `marin-community/marin_moe`, prefix `ra2a-mw-h*`

## Decision Log

## Conclusion

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 First arms scored (steps 5–24 means, hero shape EP64, one rack each):

- h01 — cf 1.15 posture baseline, safe flags: 19.61% MFU, 216.7k tok/s, zero drops. The drop-safe capacity costs 0.59 MFU points against g17's cf 1.00.
- h02 — h01 + latency-hiding scheduler + overlap limit 4: 20.00% MFU, 221.0k tok/s, zero drops, finite loss identical to h01. The first-backward corruption that forced the ragged safe flags does not reproduce on the kmax128/dev20260811 generation, so latency hiding + overlap 4 is the new ragged default (+0.39 points).

The remaining ~5-point gap is structural. In flight: h05 (XProf anatomy of the h02 config) and h03 (splits-per-peer 32→16; 32 was tuned at EP16 where per-peer slices are 4× larger). Queued: command buffers at the #8277 capture set, then whatever the trace indicts.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Transport-lever update. The splits ladder is sealed (16 worse, 32≈64 tied at 20.0% MFU) and 16-byte stores in the symmetric kernel are flat (h08, 20.12%), so the residual 4.0 s/step transport cost is structural to the symmetric-kernel-plus-external-barriers path.

The promising alternative is upstream's newer fused one-shot (`--xla_gpu_experimental_ragged_all_to_all_use_device_kernel`): one kernel per collective, 512 threads/CTA, 16-byte vectors, in-kernel NCCL LSA barrier. A 4-node probe (`ra2a-mw-h10-ep16-e48-devkernel-vlog-20260815`) shows it engages and then dies on exactly the openxla/xla#47146 gate: `RET_CHECK failure (ragged_all_to_all_thunk.cc:943) peer_access_enabled` — a CUDA-P2P check that the NVL72 window mapping does not need (the symmetric kernel already does cross-node `ncclGetLsaPointer` writes in every passing run). The same check inside the thunk's command-buffer `Record()` path is the most economical explanation for the five compile-phase crashes that retired the command-buffer arm.

A one-line gate relax in the self-built PJRT wheel would unblock both arms; it needs a human go (the session's permission tooling declines to script removal of a RET_CHECK). In flight meanwhile: HBM-resident optimizer state at mem fraction 0.90 (h11) and a trace verifying the 16-byte kernel engagement (h12).

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Day-one synthesis after 12 arms. Frontier: 20.0–20.1% MFU / ~221k tok/s at the drop-safe posture (cf 1.15, zero in-harness drops), from 20.20% at cf 1.00. The `rl1` real-LR drop-trajectory run (300 steps, 3000-step schedule) is queued to demonstrate the <2% steady-state criterion empirically.

Sealed levers: splits 16/32/64 (flat), 16-byte stores (kernel −24%, end-to-end flat — the transport is largely overlapped under latency hiding), command buffers (deterministic compile-phase crash, five attempts), HBM-resident optimizer state (109 GiB slab OOM at mem fraction 0.90).

Remaining mapped headroom, in order of size:

1. Fused one-shot device kernel — blocked only by the openxla/xla#47146 CUDA-P2P gate (exact error captured in `ra2a-mw-h10`); a one-line gate relax in the self-built wheel unblocks it and likely the command-buffer arm too (same RET_CHECK in the thunk's Record path). Removes 0.56 s/step of barrier launches plus the exposed transport tail. Needs a human go.
2. Expert grouped-GEMM efficiency: ~4.5 s/step at ~40% efficiency vs ~65% for the dense path's nvjet batched GEMMs. A ragged-transport + capacity-padded dense expert-compute backend would trade ~15% padding FLOPs for nvjet efficiency (~1.3 s/step estimate; levanter code work, no fidelity change).
3. Tile retunes (cuDNN wgrad, QuACK) at the i3072 hero shapes: ≤0.5 s combined.

Context: at the true 8/384 shape, ragged 20.1% at ~0% drops is already the strongest measured configuration (fixed reached 18.6% at ~25% drops; the pooled-wave probes have not yet logged a completed run). The ~25%/~300k reference numbers correspond to the fixed template at its E192 shapes.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Critical-path analysis of the h05 trace (merged stream intervals, per step): compute stream busy 13.5 s, collective stream busy 3.85 s of which 3.22 s is exposed (compute idle underneath) — ragged kernels 1.33 s busy / 96% exposed, barriers 0.52 s / 87% exposed, remaining NCCL ~2.0 s. Device idle plus offload staging accounts for the last ~2 s of the 19 s step. The earlier "4.0 s/step ragged" figure was a summary artifact; the merged timeline is authoritative.

Two consequences. First, vec16's kernel win (−0.32 s/step exposed) is probably real and was masked by cross-rack placement variance in the h12 draw — small-delta arms need same-rack pairing. Second, the padded-dense backend result splits by shape: it beat the EP16/i6272 record on its first run (`h13`: 22.56% MFU, zero drops, at the drop-safe posture) but regressed at the hero's i3072 (`h14`: 19.84% vs grouped 20.00%) — unfused SwiGLU materializations and window gather/scatter eat the GEMM-efficiency gain at the thinner shape. It stays in the tree as `ep-ragged-dense` (its per-expert-cap drops measured 0.01–0.09% at cf 1.15).

Where the remaining ~3.8 s to 25% actually lives: exposed collectives ~3.2 s (fused device kernel + pipelining — the gate-relax decision), compute-stream efficiency (13.5 s at ~29% aggregate; the elementwise/fusion tail, not the GEMMs, is the drag), and the staging/idle ~2 s (offload overlap, levanter code work).

Operational: gangs needing fresh compilation died at ~50% tonight in a leader-node coordination-service death with swallowed stderr (h04a–e, h06, h09/h09b, rl1/rl1b); cache-warm gangs all passed. The shared object-store JAX compilation cache is the suspect (same machinery as the earlier clique-hang incident); `rl1c` is retrying the real-LR drop-trajectory run with a per-run cache dir as the workaround probe.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 The <2% steady-state drop criterion is demonstrated at the hero shape. `ra2a-mw-rl1c-ep64-e384-k8-cf115-realLR-droptraj-20260815` completed 300 real-LR steps (3000-step schedule) at cf 1.15 on the grouped ragged backend: drops over steps 250–299 averaged 0.107% with a worst step of 0.254%, still declining — more than 8× margin under budget. The router-collapse transient peaked at 24% around step 11 and fell below 2% by step 54, matching the EP16 r-series shape. Final loss 2.959.

Operational confirmation: rl1c ran with a per-run `JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR` and survived where its two shared-cache twins died pre-step-0 — one clean data point for the shared-compilation-cache gang-mortality hypothesis. The campaign now rotates the cache dir on every fresh-compile arm.

Next: the gate-relax PJRT wheel (openxla/xla#47146 check removed, user-approved) is building; the fused device-kernel arm follows it.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Gate-relax outcome and day-one close.

The user-approved wheel (kMaxPeers=128 + 16-byte stores + the #47146 peer-access check removed from RunCollective) builds and runs: h15 completed with finite loss and zero drops where every prior device-kernel attempt crashed. The h16 trace confirms `RaggedAllToAllDeviceKernelImpl<16l>` engages and all MultiGpuBarrier launches disappear — but the fused kernel costs ~19.4 ms per collective (3.07 s/step, 91% exposed): the in-kernel world barrier folds 64-rank skew into a stream-blocking kernel. Upstream's fused one-shot is structurally unprofitable at this scale, so the transport lane is now fully explored: splits, store width, padded-dense expert compute, and the device kernel all measure flat or worse than the symmetric-kernel + external-barrier path.

One keep fell out of the trace: `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_nccl_symmetric_buffers=true` alone (h17b) gains +0.20 MFU points (4σ) by replacing the ring AllGathers with LDMC/STMC multimem kernels.

Day-one frontier: **20.20% MFU / 223.2k tok/s at cf 1.15 with zero in-harness drops** (`ra2a-mw-h17b-...`), and 0.107% steady-state drops demonstrated with real LR (rl1c). Cumulative from the posture baseline: +0.59 points. Remaining mapped headroom toward 25%: the compute stream's ~29% aggregate efficiency (elementwise/fusion tail, not the GEMMs) and the ~2 s/step staging/idle band — both code work rather than launch knobs.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 **Configuration phase complete — frontier 20.20% MFU / 223k tok/s at zero drops, and the step is compute-bound.**

Nineteen arms explored the full launch-knob / flag / self-built-wheel space. Kept configuration: cf 1.15, latency-hiding scheduler + collective overlap 4, `--xla_gpu_ragged_all_to_all_mode=symmetric` + `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_nccl_symmetric_buffers=true`, splits-per-peer 32, the kMaxPeers-128 + 16-byte-store wheel, mem fraction 0.68, and a per-run compilation cache dir. The `<2%` steady-state drop half of the goal is met with margin: 0.107% at real LR (`rl1c`).

Why 20.2% is the configuration ceiling: the EP64 hero step is compute-bound. The compute stream runs 13.5 s/step at ~29% of model-FLOP peak, and every collective, backward recompute, and optimizer-staging copy overlaps under it — merged device idle is only ~0.54 s/step. That is why every lever measured flat:

| lever | result |
|---|---|
| splits-per-peer 8/16/32/64 | flat, 32 best |
| 16-byte symmetric-kernel stores | −24% kernel time, e2e flat (overlapped) |
| padded-dense expert GEMMs (`ep-ragged-dense`, committed) | +0.5 pts at EP16, −0.15 at hero i3072 |
| fused device kernel (gate-relax wheel, user-approved) | engages, but −3 pts (in-kernel 64-rank barrier blocks the stream) |
| command buffers | deterministic compile crash |
| HBM-resident optimizer state | 109 GiB OOM |
| `save_moe` remat | throughput-neutral (recompute already hidden); correctness untestable at LR≈0 |

The remaining ~3.8 s/step to 25% lives entirely in the compute stream: the QuACK activation GEMMs (~9 s/step, the largest single item), the SwiGLU/permute fusion tail, and ~36k/step tiny D2D copies from the sort/gather `custom_vjp`. That is kernel and fusion work, not configuration.

Target-definition note for whoever picks this up: the 25% / 300k reference is the fixed template at **E192/i3072** — a smaller model (24.5 B active). At the true **8/384** hero shape the fixed transport has no completed run (the pooled-wave 8/384 attempts logged zero steps), so ragged's 20.2% at zero drops is the only measured hero-shape result on any transport, and it already beats fixed's iso-shape 18.6%-at-~25%-drops.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Compute-lane tuning of the stock ragged path (orthogonal to the marin-ep fused transport) banks +1.43 MFU points at the full 8/384 hero EP64 on one NVL72 rack, with no model change and no new quantization.

A merged-interval decomposition of the hero compute stream (14.8 s/step) shows GEMMs are 57.7% of it (8.55 s/step) and sit on the exposed compute path, so GEMM tuning translates end to end — unlike every transport knob, which overlaps under latency hiding and measured flat. Two scheduling-only QuACK knobs, each screened on one GB200 and confirmed at the hero shape:

- Activation-GEMM tile (256,256) vs the generic (256,128): +0.83 pts. h20 = 21.03% MFU / 232k tok/s.
- CLC persistence at that tile: a further +0.60 pts. h21 = 21.63% MFU / 239k tok/s.

Trajectory: 20.20% -> 21.03% -> 21.63% MFU, 223k -> 239k tok/s. Drops zero and loss bit-identical (11.806) at every step, confirming both changes are scheduling-only.

Remaining gap to the 25% / 300k target (~3.4 pts / ~61k tok/s) is structural, not tuning: the 3.2 s/step exposed transport (marin-ep's fused Mosaic-GPU dispatch/combine, tracked separately) and the 5.15 s/step non-GEMM fusion/permute tail (~30 small fusions, a levanter code target). The QuACK GEMM knobs (tile, cluster, swizzle, CLC) are exhausted; nvjet dense GEMMs are cuBLASLt-autotuned; cuDNN wgrad is already tile-optimal.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Expert-group pipelining does not recover the exposed transport, and the reason is SM contention rather than scheduling.

**Result.** Two hero EP64 arms differing only in group count, so the capacity scheme and implementation cancel:

| arm | MFU (steps 5-24) | sd | drops | loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| h22 pooled capacity, tuned (prior frontier) | 21.82% | 0.07 | 0% | 11.80622 |
| h25 pipelined M=1 | 21.61% | 0.16 | 0.013% | 11.80660 |
| h26 pipelined M=2 | 21.69% | 0.31 | 0.013% | 11.80660 |

h26 - h25 = +0.08 points. The predicted gain was +2-3 points from hiding part of the 3.22 s/step exposed transport.

**Diagnosis.** Reading the scheduled HLO at M in {1,2,4} (4 GB200s, hero XLA flags): every async collective pair has real work scheduled inside it (10/10, 18/18, 34/34), and pipelining raised the total hidden work 59 -> 161 -> 313, i.e. 2.7x at M=2 and 5.3x at M=4. Scheduled overlap increased several-fold while wall clock stayed flat. That is contention for a shared resource, not a dependency stall or a conservative scheduler.

The resource is SMs. The symmetric-memory ragged all-to-all is a device kernel, and `splits-per-peer=32` was adopted precisely because it inflates its grid from 8 to 2048 blocks. An SM-saturating collective cannot hide behind SM-hungry expert GEMMs; the device time-slices and step length is unchanged. This also explains the earlier collective-overlap-limit wash, and the h05 anatomy where only 0.637 of 3.855 s/step of collective was overlapped.

**Corrected critical-path budget** (merged intervals per stream, GPU:0, 3 steps). The xprof summary's `gap_before_ops` sums gaps per track across overlapping streams and overstates them by more than an order of magnitude, which had inflated the idle bucket in earlier notes:

| bucket | s/step | share |
|---|---|---|
| compute (merged) | 13.523 | 77.1% |
| collective exposed | 3.218 | 18.4% |
| device idle | 0.538 | 3.1% |
| span | 17.535 | |

Idle is 0.54 s/step, not the ~1.6 previously recorded, so optimizer-staging overlap is worth about 0.67 MFU points rather than two. Exposed transport is close to the only bucket with the magnitude to reach 25%: driving it to zero takes the span to ~14.3 s and lands near 26.7%.

**Also validated.** Per-expert capacity is free relative to pooled (h25 is within the +/-0.5 point placement floor of h22) at 0.013% drops and unchanged loss. The pipelined path is correct: forward bit-identical to the un-chunked path and to the pooled reference, input gradients exact, and weight-gradient differences are bf16 reduction-order noise (median relative difference 0.0, large max on a few cancellation-heavy entries) confirmed across both weight-gradient backends.

**Open arms.** h27 and h28 test splits-per-peer 8 and 16 at M=2. Splits was only ever tuned at M=1, where overlap was structurally impossible, so it was optimized for isolated transport speed; if the transport is SM-bound, a lower split count is slower alone but leaves headroom for the GEMMs it now overlaps. Flat or worse closes the lever class.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Calibration points for the marin-ep L1 event simulator, from the hardware result above.

`experiments/marin_ep/perfmodel/eventsim.py` documents its own relevant limit: "compute is one serial resource per device (no SM-level split between transport and MMA warps yet)". Transport and compute are independent resources there, so overlap is free by construction. The measurements above say that assumption is load-bearing rather than cosmetic for the stock XLA transport.

`hero_l1_report()` at the hero shape predicts, per layer: fwd bulk 23.36 ms -> full 17.88 ms, bwd bulk 40.68 -> full 35.21, about 1.21x from overlap alone. On hardware, going from one expert group to two moved the step +0.4% (21.61% -> 21.69% MFU), while the scheduled HLO shows hidden work rising 2.7x. Not a like-for-like comparison, since `full` is tile-granular inside the fused transport and the hardware arm is two coarse XLA groups, but the model credits a mechanism that produced nothing on the stock path.

Three points to calibrate against:

1. Realized overlap on the stock transport is 0.637 of 3.855 s/step, i.e. 16.5%, from merged per-stream intervals on the h05 trace. Compute is 13.523 s/step, so under independent resources nearly all of the collective could hide.
2. Raising scheduled overlap 2.7x (M=1 -> M=2) and 5.3x (M=4) left realized throughput flat.
3. Step span 17.535 s/step decomposes as union busy 16.997 plus idle 0.538, with the collective contributing only its exposed 3.218 to the union.

The implication is specific to the baseline, not to the fused design: `bulk` is documented as approximating today's XLA all-to-all schedule shape, and on hardware that schedule neither pays the full serialization `bulk` assumes nor recovers what `full` predicts when pipelined. For the fused kernel the assumption is closer to sound, because the warp split between transport and MMA is owned explicitly (MEP-045 measured the GEMM hiding fully inside the transport kernel). Calibrating the overlap credit on these points would tighten the measured advantage attributed to the fused transport.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Final arm: the splits x M interaction is negative, which closes the last in-scope lever.

| arm | M | splits | MFU | sd | drops |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| h26 | 2 | 32 | 21.6948% | 0.309 | 0.0134% |
| h29 | 2 | 8 | 21.0736% | 0.128 | 0.0134% |

Splits 8 is 0.62 points worse at the same group count, and the confound runs the other way since h29 carries the threaded-combine-buffer fix and h26 does not. The hypothesis was that a lower split count trades isolated transport speed for SM headroom the overlapping GEMMs could use. It loses on both counts.

**Conclusion: the stock ragged all-to-all path tops out near 22% MFU at the 8/384 hero shape. Frontier is 21.82% (h22) at zero drops with bit-identical loss, against a 25% gate.**

Lever ledger for the campaign:

| lever | result |
|---|---|
| QuACK GEMM tile / swizzle / CLC persistence / per-callsite cluster | +1.62 points banked, 20.20 -> 21.82, knobs exhausted |
| Redundant backward padded-row masks | provably bit-identical, sub-noise end to end |
| LHS collective overlap limit 4 -> 8 | wash |
| Expert-group pipelining, M=2 | wash, +0.08 |
| splits x M, splits 8 at M=2 | negative, -0.62 |
| Per-expert capacity vs pooled | free at 0.0134% drops; enabling, not a gain |
| Capacity factor 1.15 -> 1.00 | about +0.6 available but spends drop budget; insufficient alone |
| Device idle, 0.538 s/step | 0.67 point ceiling, step-boundary sync |

Even an optimistic remainder of capacity plus perfect idle recovery reaches about 23.1%.

The mechanism is the SM contention documented in the previous comment. The step is compute 13.523 s plus exposed collective 3.218 s plus idle 0.538 s, and only 16.5% of collective time overlaps compute. That fraction cannot be raised from above the kernel: the symmetric-memory ragged all-to-all is an SM-consuming device kernel contending with the expert GEMMs it would have to hide behind, which is why raising scheduled overlap 2.7x changed nothing and why shrinking its grid made things worse. Driving exposed transport to zero is worth about 4.9 points and would clear the gate, but it requires owning the SM and warp split between transport and MMA, i.e. a fused persistent transport plus GEMM kernel. That is the marin-ep M7b direction, out of scope here.

Fidelity and drop targets were met throughout with wide margin: 0.0134% drops at per-expert capacity against a 2% budget, no model change, no new quantization, loss unchanged at 11.8066. The small-scale loss validation remains unrun because its gate is the throughput target.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Leg-2 result: the ragged transport now beats pooled-wave on throughput, drops, and loss.

The structural rewrite (branch `research/mcwitt/8317-ragged-tune`) replaces the ragged backend's repeat/sort/compact/local-permute machinery with expert-granular `ragged_all_to_all` updates: senders read accepted prefixes at unclipped offsets, receiver offsets pack arrivals expert-major, and the dispatch buffer is built with one gather. The lean graph could not run unchunked — XLA never rematerializes collectives, so the exposed a2a outputs pinned 192–194 GiB against 184 GiB HBM across four launch postures — and landing it required processing local experts in two sequential chunks with per-chunk capacity, plus a splits-per-peer retune to 64.

Hero shape, one NVL72 rack, synthetic 15-min protocol, same-night pair: **22.80 MFU vs 21.16 old-ragged baseline (+7.7%) and vs 22.31 pooled-wave**, dropless, loss in the established band. Trace anatomy of the keep: compute is now below pooled's (the ~1.1 s/step permutation win landed), and the residual gap to 25% is ~2.4 s/step of fully exposed collectives — every scheduling lever for which is closed with a mechanism (latency-hiding scheduler adds ~9 GiB of scheduled liveness and OOMs at chunks 2 and 3; chunk pipelining fits but ties on SM contention; command buffers and the post-#47263 device kernel tie; dropping the chunk barrier regresses).

Validation (`small_scale_abl_launch.py` grew a `ragged` flavor; d768, gb200-rack EP64, harrier 2026.08.17.1, 10,827 steps, identical settings): ragged final train loss 1.9393 vs pooled 1.9556, eval/bpb 0.9749 vs 1.0334, macro_bpb 1.0562 vs 1.1110, steady-state drops 0.031% mean / 0.20% max vs pooled's 2.69% / 3.65% — the <2% criterion met with ~60× margin under a trained router and the stricter per-chunk gate.

Two side findings: the 4-GPU `ragged_ep_check` had never been run and its `ring` ground truth is itself broken (#8578); the check now gates on an exact fp32 dense arbiter, which the new backend passes at bf16 noise. Full per-arm ledger in `autoresearch/loop-260821-leg2/` on the branch.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Two follow-up results: the realistic-regime A/B and the patch-free runtime question.

**Checkpoint-restore A/B at the hero shape** (both arms restored from the live hero's step-6000 permanent checkpoint, real mixture data, trained router, master folded into device params, same rack, 15-minute windows scored on relative steps 3–13): ragged (chunked lean path, splits 64) 22.46 MFU with 0.015% mean / 0.032% max drops; pooled-wave control 22.52 MFU with 2.67% mean / 2.84% max drops. Throughput is a statistical tie in this regime (σ≈0.5 on real data) and the drop gap is two orders of magnitude, with ragged's loss marginally ahead (1.4491 vs 1.4536 at step 6013). This is the drop-rate criterion demonstrated in the regime it was written for. Getting here fixed two latent bugs in the restore fold (`_tree_to_memory_kind` needs the concrete array sharding outside traces and the aval sharding under them).

**Patch-free runtime 2×2** (device kernel vs one-shot across runtimes, EP64): wheel one-shot 22.78, wheel device-kernel 22.72, wheel dk+`nccl_symmetric_buffers` 19.19, self-built unpatched-main dk+symbuf 19.16, official dev20260821 nightly dk+symbuf 19.40. The regression is the symmetric-buffers flag (~3.5 points on the chunked graph; it was +0.2 on the old structure), not the device-kernel source or build config — but current main's device kernel only engages when operands resolve in the registered symmetric arena, so the zero-patch configuration is shackled to that tax. The released 0.11.0 jaxlib has no viable path at all (dk faults pre-fix-vintage; the NCCL send/recv fallback compiles then deadlocks at step 1). Practical upshot: the fast path's custom-wheel dependency is now exactly one unmerged line (openxla/xla#47283, kMaxPeers 32→128) — upstreaming that beats paying 15% throughput for patch-freedom. Build recipes for the wheels are now recorded on the branch (`autoresearch/loop-260821-leg2/build_pjrt_*.sh`).

comments.author: mcwitt-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Re-measured communication/compute overlap on the current hero code. Realized overlap is now about 60% of collective time, up from 16.5% on Aug 17, and exposed collectives fell from 3.22 to 1.51 s/step. SM contention no longer explains the remaining exposed ragged transport. Most of it comes from the per-layer chunk barrier in the ragged backend.

Setup (measured): One GB200 NVL72 rack (16 × 4 GPUs, EP64), `hero-fa4sm100-nomask-step146k` recipe at main `8d70d9cbb0` (contains `ad754c6d67` / #9378), restored from the hero's `step-144000`, real mixture data, batch 1024, production `XLA_FLAGS` and `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION`, coordinated GC every 100 steps. XProf on rank 0 (GPU:0) for steps 144010–144012. Run: [overlap-remeasure-main-144k](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/overlap-remeasure-main-144k), Iris job `/mwittmann/overlap-remeasure-main-144k-coord`. This trace covers only rack-local collectives, as h05 did. Step 144010 is a watch step (norm collection every 10 steps), so the steady-state columns below average steps 144011–144012. The trace spans match W&B `throughput/duration` (14.20 vs 14.00 s and 13.86 vs 13.86 s).

Method: Same as the h05 anatomy: merged intervals within each step on GPU:0. A step is the device window between consecutive host launches of `jit_train_step`. Kernels are classified by name and HLO op, because some FSDP all-gathers run on the compute stream. Exposed collective = union of collective kernels minus union of compute kernels. Realized overlap = 1 − exposed/busy. Idle = span minus the union of all kernels and memcpys. The literal per-stream variant (compute stream #17 vs collective stream #83) is also listed.

| per step, 1 rack | Aug 17 h05 (measured) | now, steady 144011–12 (measured) | now, watch step 144010 (measured) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| step span | 17.535 s | 14.031 s | 15.256 s |
| compute busy (merged) | 13.523 s | 11.787 s | 11.807 s |
| collective busy (merged) | 3.855 s | 3.806 s | 4.264 s |
| collective exposed | 3.218 s | 1.505 s | 2.032 s |
| realized overlap | 16.5% | 60.5% | 52.3% |
| memcpy only (offload staging, nothing else running) | ~0.26 s (residual) | 0.619 s | 0.626 s |
| device idle | 0.538 s | 0.120 s | 0.790 s |
| per-stream variant: exposed / overlap | 3.218 s / 16.5% | 1.255 s / 64.7% | 1.796 s / 55.4% |

The kernel-classified and per-stream figures differ by the 0.25 s/step of all-gathers issued on the compute stream. Those are exposed by construction.

Collective time by type, steady state, measured, s/step:

| type | busy | exposed | crosses racks in the 11-rack job |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| ragged all-to-all dispatch/combine (`RaggedAllToAllDeviceKernelImpl<16>`) | 2.171 | 0.805 | no, `expert` axis is rack-local |
| FSDP all-gather, async on collective stream | 1.009 | 0.259 | no, (`data`, `expert`) is rack-local |
| FSDP all-gather, sync on compute stream (`all-gather.127.remat` + 2 small sites) | 0.251 | 0.251 | no |
| FSDP reduce-scatter | 0.115 | 0.060 | no |
| all-reduce: router QB `pmin`/`pmax`/`psum_invariant` histogram, drop count | 0.10 | 0.04 | yes, reduced over `token_axes`, which include `replica_dcn` |
| all-reduce: other (norms, loss, misc) | 0.09 | 0.07 | partly |
| NCCL all-to-all (`SendRecv`) | 0.076 | 0.017 | no |
| gradient reduction over `replica_dcn` | absent at 1 rack | absent | yes |

The one-rack trace cannot see the cross-rack gradient reduction. Production over steps 146139–150632 has a median `throughput/duration` of 14.71 s at 26.68% MFU (measured, 11 racks). The one-rack median over steps 144010–144015 is 13.96 s. The difference, about 0.75 s/step, bounds the cross-rack collectives plus 704-GPU straggler effects. This is a projection; a two-rack trace would attribute it.

Changes since Aug 17: Compute fell 1.74 s/step. The expert-granular backend (#8549) removed the permute and compaction work. QuACK without PDL (#9183), native SM100 FA4 (#9332) and tail-mask removal (#9333) contributed the rest. The step-level A/Bs in those PRs attribute the gains; this trace does not split them. Collective busy time is about the same (3.86 vs 3.81 s), but its composition changed. Ragged transport busy time rose from 1.33 to 2.17 s. The backend now issues 12 transports per layer: 2 chunks × dispatch/combine × forward, recompute and backward. No separate barrier kernels appear in this trace (h05 had 0.52 s/step of them). The balanced-CTA wheel (#9179) is the main reason for the higher overlap. The ragged kernel now launches 32 CTAs × 512 threads (theoretical occupancy 25%, so at most 32 of 148 SMs), where the Aug kernel used `splits-per-peer=32` and a 2048-block grid. Ragged exposure fell from 96% to 37% of its busy time.

SM contention: For each compute kernel (same name and launch geometry), I compared the median duration of instances with no collective overlap against instances that overlap a collective for at least half their duration. Kernels overlapping the ragged transport run 18.7% longer on average (for example `nvjet_sm100_tst_256x192` 1.41 → 1.96 ms). That matches the 32/148 = 22% of SMs the transport holds. The cost is 0.20 s/step, against 1.37 s/step of ragged time now hidden. Kernels overlapping NCCL collectives run 3–5% longer. Contention therefore takes about 0.15 s of compute per second of hidden transport, and does not stop overlap. Occupancy here comes from CUPTI launch geometry (grid, block, registers, shared memory) and XProf's theoretical occupancy. I did not collect Nsight SM-active counters.

Location of the exposed ragged transport: Exposure concentrates at 4 of 12 call sites per layer. Fully exposed: `ragged-all-to-all.8.1` and `.9.1` (forward, 0.34 s/step) and `.13` and `.1.1` (backward, 0.33 s/step), 99–100% each. The other 8 sites are 0–24% exposed, 0.13 s/step in total. From execution order, `.8.1` is chunk 0's dispatch and `.9.1` is chunk 0's combine; the backward pair is the same. In the forward timeline of one layer, chunk 0's dispatch runs with the compute stream idle (3.4 ms). The chunk-0 expert GEMMs follow (8.8 ms), and the collective stream is idle underneath them. Chunk 0's combine then runs exposed (3.4 ms). Chunk 1's dispatch overlaps the routing sort and the dense shared-path GEMMs (about 6 ms). Chunk 1's combine overlaps later work. The cause is `optimization_barrier((sorted_x, returned))` in [`ep_ragged_all_to_all.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8d70d9cbb0/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py#L386-L391). The barrier makes chunk c+1's dispatch wait for chunk c's combine. Its comment says a variant that overlaps one transport with the MLP fits in memory but is no faster because "the transport and the MLP compete for the same SMs". That result was measured on the 2048-block kernel (h25/h26 in the Aug 17 comment), before #9179.

MFU headroom, projected from step time (MFU scales with 1/step time):

- All rack-local exposed collectives at zero (−1.505 s): one rack 28.2% → 31.5%. Eleven racks 26.68% → 29.7%.
- The same plus the ~0.75 s eleven-rack surplus at zero: eleven racks → 31.5%.

Levers, most credible first (eleven-rack projections, before re-measurement):

1. Relax the chunk barrier so chunk 1's dispatch overlaps chunk 0's GEMMs and chunk 0's combine overlaps chunk 1's GEMMs. The target is the 0.67 s/step at the four fully exposed sites. Chunk 0's combine would hide under chunk 1's GEMMs directly. Chunk 0's dispatch hides only if the scheduler moves the shared-path GEMMs under it, as it now does for chunk 1's dispatch. At the measured 0.15 s contention cost per hidden second, the net is about 0.57 s if all four hide (26.68% → ~27.8%) and about 0.28 s if only the combines hide (→ ~27.2%). The barrier exists for HBM, so the overlap-one-transport variant must be re-validated for memory and loss on the current wheel.
2. Stop rematerializing `all-gather.127`, or prefetch it asynchronously. It is 48 synchronous all-gathers per step on the compute stream, 0.23 s/step fully exposed. That gives ~27.1%.
3. The remaining async FSDP all-gather/reduce-scatter exposure is 0.32 s/step (≤ +0.6 pt). It is limited by collective overlap = 1, which the README says must stay at 1 for correctness with the carry offload. Low confidence.
4. Memcpy-only offload staging is 0.62 s/step of host-device copies with no kernel running. After exposed collectives it is the largest non-compute bucket (≤ +1.2 pt if hidden).
5. Attribute the ~0.75 s eleven-rack surplus with a two-rack profile before acting on the cross-rack collectives.

Levers 1 and 2 together project to 27.6–28.2% on eleven racks.

<details><summary>Decomposition core (per step, GPU:0 XPlane)</summary>

```python
# classes: kernel -> "compute" | "coll:<type>" | "memcpy" (by kernel name + hlo_op)
comp = merge(clip(classes["compute"], lo, hi))
coll = merge([iv for c in classes if c.startswith("coll:") for iv in clip(classes[c], lo, hi)])
everything = merge([iv for c in classes for iv in clip(classes[c], lo, hi)])
exposed = length(coll) - length(intersect(coll, comp))
overlap_pct = 100 * (1 - exposed / length(coll))
idle = (hi - lo) - length(everything)
# step windows [lo, hi): consecutive host "CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::Execute (jit_train_step)" starts;
# the last window ends at the last device event of jit_train_step.
```

</details>

Done when:

- A recipe version identifies its parent checkpoint, tokenizer and chat template, data mixture and immutable revisions, training configuration, and export contract.
- The recipe has acceptance evaluations for every listed competency, with recorded baseline comparisons and failure criteria.
- The recipe can be run after a pretraining cool-down without experiment-specific manual wiring.
- The selected recipe and its evidence are documented in the repository.

issues.title: [epic][sft] Establish a versioned cold-start SFT recipe

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
## Goal

Honest replication of the paper's base-size experiment (Table 6) with a dense model: d8 (width 1024, ~210M params, vocab 50,304), 1B tokens of FineWeb with the GPT-2 tokenizer, batch 524,288, 2048-token sequences, under the paper's own Table 5 hyperparameters.

Three arms (branch `paper-replication`, variant `experiments/grug/paper_rep/`):

| Arm | Model | Recipe | Paper target (val loss) | Ours |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vanilla` | plain transformer | Vanilla | 3.3279 | 3.2661 |
| `op1` | Operator-1 (K=1, 2/3/3 split, alpha 1) | Operator-1 | 3.3057 | 3.4738 |
| `op1-vanilla-recipe` | Operator-1 | Vanilla | 3.3135 | 3.2561 |

**Result:** the transfer probe replicates (Operator-1 under the vanilla recipe is −0.010 better than vanilla; paper: −0.014), but the central claim does not — the Operator-1 own recipe is +0.208 worse than vanilla instead of −0.022 better. Full analysis in the verdict comment below.

**1000-step screening follow-up:** The WTE/UIS pair explains 92% of the init-cluster penalty at step 1000 (+0.283 eval loss over the screen base); RM/OM contributes +0.011 alone. The split does not identify which of WTE and UIS matters most. [Runs and analysis](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9292#issuecomment-5823758637).

## Context

- Variant PR: #9293
- The MoE-vehicle ablation (#9280) showed the paper's recipe knobs (ELRM/HLRM/RM/OM/WTE/UIS/WD) do not exist in the MuonH template, which motivated this dense replication under the paper's own optimizer.
- Documented deviations (WD placement, Muon internals, the FineWeb 10BT slice, sequence packing) are listed in the variant README.

## Plan

- [x] Implement variant (`model.py`, `optimizer.py`, `recipes.py`, `data.py`, `train.py`, `launch.py`, tests)
- [x] Lint + tests green; PR open
- [x] Materialize FineWeb caches (one-time download + tokenize)
- [x] Run the three arms (~45 min each)
- [x] Compare against Table 6 and record the verdict (with W&B run links)

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 **Result: dense replication of the base-size experiment (d8, 1B tokens) — the architecture gain replicates, the Operator-1 own-recipe gain does not.**

All three arms completed (1907 steps, batch 524,288 tokens, seed 0, shared FineWeb caches, preemptible v4-16, ~45 min each). Final eval loss on the held-out FineWeb file (`eval/loss`, micro-average over 200×256×2048 ≈ 105M tokens):

| Arm | Ours | Paper (Table 6) | Δ ours−paper |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vanilla | **3.2661** | 3.3279 | −0.062 |
| Operator-1, own recipe | **3.4738** | 3.3057 | +0.168 |
| Operator-1, vanilla recipe | **3.2561** | 3.3135 | −0.057 |

Eval-loss trajectories (steps 500 / 1000 / 1500 / 1907):

- vanilla: 3.7407 / 3.4931 / 3.3381 / 3.2661
- op1, own recipe: 4.1686 / 3.7217 / 3.5456 / 3.4738
- op1, vanilla recipe: 3.7563 / 3.4988 / 3.3317 / 3.2561

## What replicates

- **The transfer probe.** Operator-1 under the vanilla recipe beats plain vanilla by −0.0100 (paper: −0.0144). The K=1 boundary operator architecture is neutral-to-slightly-positive at this scale, matching the paper's direction and magnitude.
- **Absolute scale.** Our vanilla is 0.06 below the paper's number — expected given the documented deviations (FineWeb 10BT slice vs the full corpus, sequence packing without cross-doc attention masking, modded-nanogpt Muon internals, decoupled WD on the AdamW groups only, TPU vs the paper's H100s).

## What does not replicate

- **The paper's central claim for Operator-1**: own-recipe 3.3057 < vanilla 3.3279 (−0.022). We get the opposite sign at 10× the magnitude: own-recipe 3.4738 = **+0.208** vs our vanilla. The arm is behind from the first eval (4.17 vs 3.74 at step 500) and the gap never closes — a hyperparameter-configuration effect, not a training collapse.
- The recipe transcription was verified against paper Table 5 three separate times (most recently against the paper source): GLR 0.04, ELRM 0.905, HLRM 0.08, RM 0.5, OM 1, α<sub>emb</sub> 1, WD 0.05, WTE 0.113, UIS 0.354, WU 0, WDR 0.8, β 0.8/0.98, ε 1e-10. The LR schedule was verified step-by-step: constant GLR from step 0 (the paper specifies no warmup for Operator-1), linear warmdown over the last 80% to zero.

## Interpretation

Consistent with the Phase-0 MoE ablation (#9280): the boundary-operator architecture does not carry a robust gain in our stack, and the paper's Operator-1 advantage is not robust to the documented implementation deviations. The own-recipe inversion (paper −0.008 recipe benefit → our +0.218 penalty) points at recipe–implementation interactions — most plausibly WU=0 with full GLR 0.04 under our Muon, or the WTE/UIS/ELRM init-scale cluster — which the paper's reported numbers do not disambiguate. A knob-at-a-time ablation of the Operator-1 recipe under our implementation would isolate it (not done here).

## Runs

- Data: train cache `fineweb-10bt-gpt2@2026.09.19` (10.34B tokens / 14.87M docs), val `fineweb-val-gpt2@2026.09.19` (400k docs / 295.8M tokens)
- Vanilla: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/paper_rep_d8_vanilla
- Operator-1 own recipe: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/paper_rep_d8_op1
- Operator-1 vanilla recipe: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/paper_rep_d8_op1_vanilla_recipe

Variant: `experiments/grug/paper_rep/` (PR #9293). Infra note: the v4-8 pools were degraded at launch time, so arms ran on preemptible v4-16 (batch 256 divides evenly; global batch and data order unchanged, all arms identical hardware).

## Screening sweep: what drives the own-recipe penalty

The full-length verdict left one question open: the Operator-1 own recipe is +0.208 worse than the same model under the vanilla recipe, behind from the first eval and partially healing — an early-training injury — but which of the recipe's knob clusters causes it? The screen flips one suspect cluster at a time between the two Table 5 columns, always on the Operator-1 model, at 1000 steps with 250-step evals. Screening runs get their own coherent schedule, so they compare only to each other.

All arms ran on one preemptible v4-32 (the v4-16 pool was in boot backoff; same zone and global batch). Eval loss:

| [`screen-wu0`](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/paper_rep_d8_screen_wu0) | Vanilla + WU=0 | 4.042 | 3.697 | 3.497 | 3.393 | −0.013 |
| [`screen-init-own`](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/paper_rep_d8_screen_init_own) | Vanilla + own WTE/UIS/RM/OM | 4.607 | 4.174 | 3.850 | 3.715 | **+0.309** |
| [`screen-opt-own`](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/paper_rep_d8_screen_opt_own) | Vanilla + own ELRM/HLRM/WD/WDR/β2 | 4.100 | 3.688 | 3.511 | 3.423 | +0.017 |
| [`screen-own-wu40`](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/paper_rep_d8_screen_own_wu40) | Operator-1 + WU=40 | 4.542 | 4.148 | 3.874 | 3.757 | +0.351 |

**Attribution: the model-side init cluster is the driver.**

- **Warmup is eliminated.** `screen-wu0` is indistinguishable from base (no-warmup at full GLR 0.04 is harmless under the vanilla recipe), and `screen-own-wu40` stays fully broken — restoring warmup does not repair the own recipe. The top suspect going in is out.
- **The optimizer cluster is neutral.** ELRM/HLRM/WD/WDR/β2 differences contribute +0.017 alone — noise.
- **The init cluster alone reproduces 84% of the penalty** (+0.309 of the +0.368 gap) and is worse than the full own recipe at the first eval (4.607 vs 4.514). The knobs: WTE 0.113 vs 0.007 (16×), UIS 0.354 vs 0.063 (5.6×), RM 0.5 vs 0.25, OM 1 vs 0.5.
- The remaining +0.06 is an interaction: the optimizer knobs add a little damage only when combined with the init cluster.

**What this means for the replication:** the own-recipe inversion is localized to the Operator-1 initialization scales as transcribed from Table 5 — a paper-recipe × our-implementation interaction, not a transcription error (verified 3×) and not the optimizer or schedule. If we want the own recipe to work in our stack, the init cluster is what to change. A second-stage split (`screen-init-embed`: WTE/UIS only vs `screen-init-depth`: RM/OM only) is queued to pin down which knobs; it is currently waiting on TPU capacity (us-central2-b provisioning has been failing all afternoon — both preemptible and reserved pools; the arms self-start when a slice comes up).

No full-length confirmation run is planned: the existing full-length arms already contain the endpoints (op1-vanilla-recipe at 3.2561 is the own recipe minus every neutral knob), and the screens show the rest of the recipe is neutral, so a full-length "own minus init" run would re-measure ≈3.25 ± noise. If wanted as belt-and-suspenders, it is one command (`--arm` with the mixed recipe added).

Recipe/diff details and the arm table are in the variant README (`experiments/grug/paper_rep/README.md`, "Screening sweep" section). Screening arms were added in 9a04d782aa (first stage) and 0858ce6c8e (second-stage split).

spillover_issues.author: gonzalobenegas
spillover_issues.body:
Generate realistic, reusable **computational-biology Harbor tasks** with executable rewards. The deliverable is task packages that others can plug into their pipelines; model training, trajectory collection, model selection and context budgets are outside this issue.

## Progress

As of 2026-09-25 ([checkpoint](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/c50a382c5a)):

| Measure | Current |
|---|---:|
| Real-data task candidates | **31**; validation and release review vary by task |
| Reviewed, validated competency assignments | **0**; draft mappings do not earn coverage |
| Repositories exercised with passing native operations | **40 / 50** |

The registry also contains **115 synthetic correctness controls**, excluded from final training. The dataset is not release-ready. Existing benchmark mappings remain provenance; they do not automatically establish competency coverage.

[Explore competencies and inspect examples](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/docs/experiments/bio-task-coverage.html). This public, version-controlled explorer distinguishes candidates, evidence and gaps.

## Coverage and task requirements

- Use eligible **agentic ID benchmarks** to derive assessable competencies and realistic workflows. Keep exact source task IDs and adaptations as provenance. Scientific areas are provisional navigation categories; single-cell, spatial, regulatory and other cross-cutting properties can be facets. **The taxonomy and allocation weights remain undecided.** For now, create tasks addressing missing benchmark-derived competencies; no uniform or demand-weighted quota has been adopted.
- Prefer real observed biological inputs, realistic sizes and connected scientific decisions. Record accessions, transformations, biological lineage and redistribution terms; keep benchmark fixtures and answers out of task inputs. Context adaptations can count when methods, decisions and complete outputs match, with the change explicit.
- Default to **one task per recipe and one train split**. There is no task-count cap or easy/medium/hard quota. Add variants only for meaningful differences in data, study design or decisions.
- Provide a private, input-reading oracle that runs the actual packages. Verify complete artifacts with explicit tolerances, independent checks and incorrect-output controls. **No LLM-as-a-judge.** Defer endpoints without useful executable scoring and retain their gaps.
- Track native formats and their semantics—FASTA/FASTQ, BED, SAM/BAM/CRAM, GFF/GTF, VCF/BCF, PDB/mmCIF, H5AD, matrices, trees and images—alongside package and competency coverage.
- Validate through **Harbor**, with pinned sandbox resources and environments, offline inputs by default, and a target solve time of **30 minutes or less**. Notebook-based benchmarks inform questions, not a separate execution protocol. Explicit retrieval tasks need bounded sources and checkable outputs.
- Make questions, input previews and sizes, provenance and validation evidence inspectable. Keep oracle answers and verifier references separate from solver-visible inputs.

Provisional ID sources include BixBench, CompBioBench, BiomniBench-DA and BioAgent. Preserve all existing OOD labels, including Terminal-Bench-Science, GeneBench, BioMysteryBench and SciCode; do not use OOD tasks for authoring.

## Current work and maintained detail

Task creation has resumed while taxonomy and weighting are reviewed separately. The count/shrinkage/enrichment workflow passed its native oracle and Harbor checks, including four rejected controls. Upcoming workflows cover single-cell normalization/PCA, BAM read structure and heme-pocket analysis. Each author owns a complete Harbor task through validation; shared verifier integration and competency review remain coordinated separately.

- [Guide and preliminary taxonomy/weighting ideas](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/docs/experiments/bio-tasks.md), [question portfolio and queue](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/docs/experiments/bio-task-queue.md).
- [Benchmark sources](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/benchmark_sources.json) and [task inventories](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/benchmark_tasks): ID/OOD policy and competency provenance.
- [Task catalog](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/docs/experiments/bio-task-catalog.md) and [original package metadata](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/docs/experiments/computational_biology_bioinformatics_packages.md): formats, repositories, downloads, stars, citations and validation evidence.

Keep this issue as the current summary; detailed plans and evidence live in the linked files. Task-generation inspiration: [arXiv:2602.21193](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21193).
