| α=1.0, LR ×0.5 | 3.5776 | 425,052 | 0.949 |
| α=1.0, LR ×2.0 | 3.6115 | 431,461 | 0.912 |

**Debug ladder (per the replication plan):**
- **α insurance**: α=1.0 wins (−5.6e-3 vs 0.707). Paper Table 5 agrees (Operator-1 αemb=1).
- **LR re-centering**: ×1.0 is the best of {0.5, 1, 2} — the May Recipe heuristic LR is already centered for this model; the paper's transfer regret is not recoverable by GLR alone. (Paper's regret comes from the full Stage-1 chain: ELRM/HLRM/RM/OM/WD/WTE/UIS/schedule/Adam — most of these knobs don't exist in the MoE template's MuonH.)
- **Split ratio**: 2/2/2 at d6 is the paper's validated optimum (even P/C/D, remainders core-then-coda; Table 4/Fig 15a show alternatives are worse).

**Verdict**: under the May Recipe MoE with the recipe transferred from the Vanilla-equivalent baseline, the boundary operator alone does **not** beat the baseline at d512 (deficit +3.8e-3 loss; throughput parity within noise — arms span 350k–431k tok/s at identical compute). This is consistent with the paper's transfer-regret finding (Table 6: Operator-1 under Vanilla's recipe loses 7.8e-3 at base size and erases the exponent improvement, Fig. 16b). It does *not* refute the paper — we measured the transferred-recipe condition by design (recipe-matched comparability with the README baselines).

**Consequences:**
- Gate 1 cannot pass (requires speedup > 1 at both d512 and d768), so d768/d1024/d1280 arms were **not** launched — saves ~35 v4-32 slice-hours of a failing protocol.
- Phase A (looping/growth) is not justified on top of a failed Phase 0: the paper's bigger gains (Untied-Grow 1.6–2.7×) compound the same recipe-transfer risk, and each ladder point is ~10× the cost of Phase 0.

**Options going forward** (needs a decision):
1. **Close as negative result** — BO alone is not a promotable recipe change for this template under recipe-matched conditions. Cheapest; PR #9281 still lands the (well-tested, off≡baseline-verified) variant for future use.
2. **Recipe refit for the BO** (paper-style Stage-1 tuning at d512: β₁/β₂/ε/warmup/WD sweeps, ~8–10 arms ≈ 13–16 slice-hours) — tests whether the regret is recoverable in this template at all before deciding on Phase A.
3. **Skip to a combined arm** (e.g. Untied-2) at one matched cell — the paper's headline gains are there, but a single arm can't separate BO-from-looping contributions without Phase 0 passing.

Artifacts: runs under W&B `marin_moe/moe-boundary`; analysis in `.agents/projects/boundary_loop.md`.

comments.body:
🤖 **d768 matched result — gate 1 splits: d512 fails on throughput, d768 passes**

[moe_boundary_compute_opt_d768_ep1_alpha1_matched](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_boundary_compute_opt_d768_ep1_alpha1_matched) (α=1.0, matched recipe, 16,875 steps, 4.4237e9 tokens = exactly the README cell) finished: **Paloma macro 3.2186** vs baseline 3.2273.

**Gate 1 table (matched recipe, α=1.0):**

| scale | variant macro | baseline macro | Δ loss | tok/s vs baseline | effective speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| d512 (3.82e17) | 3.5415 | 3.5422 | **−0.0007** | 393,000 vs 433,986 (−9.4%) | 0.909 ✗ |
| d768 (2.81e18) | 3.2186 | 3.2273 | **−0.0087** | 285,558 vs 294,726 (−3.1%) | **1.026 ✓** |

Reading:

- **The recipe, not the operator, caused the exploratory deficits.** Both matched arms tie-or-beat baseline on loss where the pre-fix runs showed +0.0038/+0.0198 deficits. The d768 exploratory gap was the batch-mismatch confound (LR √2 too high) plus the LR floor, both now fixed.

- **d768 passes**: the loss gain (−0.0087, same order as the paper's Operator-1 transfer-regret 7.8e-3) outweighs the remaining −3.1% throughput cost. The overhead amortizes with scale and the loss advantage grows with scale — both in the paper's reported direction.

Under the original gate-1 wording (effective speedup > 1 at d512 **and** d768), the boundary operator fails at d512 alone. Whether to treat the d512 throughput penalty as a small-scale artifact that the d768 pass outgrows — i.e. continue to the d1024 gate-2 cell — is the next decision. The d768 evidence (loss advantage growing with scale, overhead shrinking) is the paper's predicted pattern, but one passing point doesn't establish a scaling trend.

🤖 **Attention Residuals (Kimi Block AttnRes, arXiv 2603.15031) — full results**

**What:** every sublayer's input is a learned softmax mix (zero-init pseudo-query, param-free/frozen RMS key norm) over completed block outputs + the running partial; Block AttnRes N=8; query on Adam at 0.1× adam lr. Flags: `--attn-res --attn-res-num-blocks 8 --attn-res-frozen-key-norm --attn-res-query-lr-scale 0.1`.

**Speed work (branch `fast-track-attn-res-ovjp`):** 0.71× → 0.95–0.98× baseline throughput. Root cause of the overhead (d768 profile, +152 ms/step): concatenating all sources into one [N+1,B,S,D] array in every gate (+64 ms), key-norm/logits over all slots (+37), weighted-sum einsums (+29), buffer copies (+13), d_blocks carry (+12). Fixes: unrolled layer loop reading only live sources; block logits computed once per completed block; per-layer custom VJP with optimization barriers (fixed a 72.9 GiB d1024 peak → 46.2 GiB). 🤖 **MLA + Relative Position Embedding (Inkling bias) — full results**

**What:** DeepSeek-V2 MLA (Q/KV low-rank latents with learnable RMSNorms, 128-dim heads) with the Inkling relative-position bias replacing RoPE (per-head content-dependent bias bank, extent 1024). QK-norm is **off** by requirement (a per-head norm on k breaks MLA's absorbed-W_UK inference). Note: in KDA/KMA configs MLA+Inkling only applies to the global layers.

**Speed work (branch `fast_track_mla_inkling`):** 0.75× → 0.91× baseline at d512, 0.72× → 0.92× at d768. Root cause: MLA is MHA; the fast Hopper backward only ran for GQA → fell back to a segmented backward + a JAX dBias pass. Fixes: sm90 MHA backward (vendored kernel supported it), fused Inkling backward default, remat saves attn out + LSE (also speeds the plain baseline +4%), banded key-aligned bias layout, gather-free bias bank, bias prefetch. GPU grad-checked (dq/dk/dv/dbias, GQA+MHA, packed segments, sliding window).

🤖 **KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) in the local layers — full results**

**What:** Kimi K3-spec KDA replaces ONLY the local sliding-window layers (global layers unchanged): separate full-width q/k/v (no GQA) + depthwise causal conv k=4 + SiLU, per-head L2 q/k, β = σ(W_b x), decay g = −5·σ(exp(A)·(W_fb W_fa x + dt_bias)), per-head RMSNorm with shared learnable scale, full-rank sigmoid output gate, W_o; hard state reset at packed-document boundaries. No sliding window (recurrent state). Best config COMBO = `--local-mixer kda --kda-dt-range 0.01,0.5 --kda-gate-opt adam --kda-beta-opt muonh`.

**Kernel work (`kda-h100-opt` → `fast-track-kda`):** fused Pallas prep + sequential Pallas state pass: 4.2× fwd / 3.2× fwd+bwd vs the XLA `chunk_kda` default (1.12 / 3.58 ms at B4 H8 L8192 d128); doc-boundary resets +5%; in-model (grug moe d512) level with SWA unpacked. comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Over-Encoding (arXiv 2501.16975) + bigram embedding — full results**

**Original branch bugs** (`fast_track_abl_over_encoding`): the n-gram hash was computed in uint32 with V=2¹⁴ — with the first table's power-of-two modulus (65536) the 3-gram id ignored x[t−2] entirely (1 distinct id over 16384 values) and the 2-gram kept only 2 bits of x[t−1]; tables 64k rows (≈4× V vs the paper's ~128× V / 12.8M); 64-wide slices (paper ≈256); each stream RMS-normalized with a shared norm (paper: plain sum ÷ (1+k(n−1))).

**Fixed (`fast-track-oe-1m`):** Horner hash with mod-m every step (split 11-bit uint32 multiply, big-int-reference tested); m = 1,048,571 (prime; never a power of two), moduli m, m+2, …; k = max(1, round(d/768)) → slices ≈256 wide; plain sum ÷ (1+k(n−1)) → existing embed norm + gate; tables Adam. 357M (d512) / 537M (d768) replicated table params; 3–6% throughput cost. **Bigram (`fast-track-bigram`):** one full-width hashed bigram table, no projection, `token + λ·bigram` with learnable scalar λ.

**Takeaway:** OE/bigram lead by ~0.01 at the midpoint but the lead vanishes by the end at d512 (tie with the 4-seed mean); fixed OE gives −0.013 at d768. λ converges to ~0.3–0.4 from any init. Remaining gaps vs the paper: 12× fewer rows, k=1 (no multi-hash), dense Adam on sparse rows (stale-momentum drift), no table-specific LR, 16k vocab (3-gram spans less text), ~30× fewer tokens/param. **Fails gate 1** as tested.

🤖 **FP8 — status (in progress, branch `fast-track-fp8`)**

**Design:** FP8 only for the large matmuls (MoE experts + attention/shared/latent projections); BF16/FP32 for embeddings, lm_head, router, norms, attention core, KDA, optimizer. Current (just-in-time) scaling, power-of-2 scales; activations/grads per-token (row-wise) E4M3, weights per-output-channel (per-expert for experts) E4M3, scales applied in the GEMM epilogue; optional FP8 MoE all-to-all dispatch (per-token scales). comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **FP8 — final write-up. Status: PARKED** (best gain ≈ +6% at d1024/d1280; not worth the complexity for now). Branch `fast-track-fp8` (local; all FP8 flags default off, BF16 unchanged, tests + lint clean).

## Bottom line
- **Quality:** every FP8 config run to the full d512 budget matched BF16 within noise (baseline 4-seed mean 3.1592, σ≈0.004).
- **Speed:** the only real win is **FP8 on the MoE all-to-all transport** (`--moe-transport fp8_dispatch_grad`: per-token E4M3 dispatch + FP8 combine output-gradient): **+3.0% d512, +5.9% d1024, +5.7% d1280**.
- **FP8 matmuls never paid through XLA**: row-wise FP8 GEMMs (dense and/or routed experts) were slower at every size; tensor-wise FP8 dense projections were ≈neutral on top of the transport win.

## Where step time goes (XProf, GPU-0 kernel ms/step)
| bucket | d512 (240 ms) | d1024 (1713 ms) | d1280 (2225 ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| routed-expert GEMMs | 13.8 (5.8%) | 148.5 (8.7%) | 232.1 (10.4%) |
| shared-expert GEMMs | 6.8 | 79.1 | 142.9 (6.4%) |
| attention q/k/v/o GEMMs | 4.2 | 52.2 | 89.1 (4.0%) |
| router + latent GEMMs | 2.5 | 26.2 | 43.1 |
| lm_head (fused CE, kept BF16) | 7.2 | 24.9 | 32.0 |
| **MoE all-to-all** | **44.7 (18.7%)** | **303.7 (17.7%)** | **418.6 (18.8%)** |
| attention core (FA4) | 16.0 | 136.7 | 201.1 |
| unscoped / optimizer / misc | ~103 (43%) | ~515 | ~700 (31%) |

FP8-eligible GEMMs are ~11% of the d512 step (ceiling ≈6% even at a perfect 2×) and memory-bound at d512 shapes; ~22% at d1280. Non-FP8 hotspots worth more than FP8 at d512: the embedding-gradient scatter-add (~14.7 ms/step, ~6%), two MoE argsorts (~6 ms each), a 13 ms transpose fusion; the d512 all-to-all runs at an effective ~35 GB/s (latency/skew-bound).

## What was implemented
- `lib/levanter/grug/fp8.py`: power-of-2, current (just-in-time) scales. **Row-wise** (per-token activations × per-output-column / per-expert weights, E4M3, scales applied after the GEMM; FP8 dgrad with `Precision.HIGHEST`, wgrad BF16) and **tensor-wise** (`FP8_TENSOR`, `FP8_TENSOR_FWD`: per-operand scale folded into the cuBLASLt FP8 GEMM). **Bound scale** for GatedNorm(RMSNorm) inputs = `sqrt(D)·max|norm weight|` (no amax pass). XLA 0.11 gotcha: `convert(f8)*scale` is *not* rewritten to an FP8 GEMM — FP8 operands must reach `dot_general` directly.
- `MoeTransport` (grug MoE EP all-to-all): `fp8_dispatch` (per-token E4M3 + int8 exponent in a 16-byte metadata column; straight-through backward) and `fp8_dispatch_grad` (+ FP8 combine output-gradient). Two per-assignment-quantized variants (FP8 combine / FP8 all) lost at d512 and d1024 and were removed.
- Flags: `--fp8-matmuls {off,dense,experts,all}`, `--fp8-dense-scaling {fp8_rowwise,fp8_tensor,fp8_tensor_fwd}`, `--moe-transport {bf16,fp8_dispatch,fp8_dispatch_grad}`, `--profile-steps`, `--seed`. Kept BF16/FP32: embedding, lm_head/CE (per request: no FP8 lm_head), router, norms, attention core, convs, optimizer.
- Bug fixed: dropless eval swapped in a local MoE backend and crashed at the step-1191 eval with FP8 formats on; now resets them (regression test added).

## Numerics tests (CPU)
Power-of-2 scale tight and 0/inf/NaN-safe; row-wise scales independent; requantize lossless; row×column rescale exactly equals a dequantized reference (fwd + grads, dense + batched); ~3.8% error vs BF16 (E4M3 rounding); tensor-wise saturates rather than NaN when a bound is exceeded; FP8 dispatch / dispatch-grad bit-exact vs BF16 on fake-quantized inputs across 11 binades; 8-device CPU model grad rel-error vs BF16 0.18% (dispatch), ~0.6% (all matmuls FP8).

## Throughput vs same-cluster BF16 (cw-rno2a probes; median of steady-state steps)
| config | d512 ex/s | Δ | d1024 ex/s | Δ | d1280 ex/s | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 baseline | 569.9 (3 runs) | – | 187.4 (2) | – | 125.0 (2) | – |
| fp8_dispatch | 580.7 (3) | +1.9% | 192.8 | +2.9% | – | – |
| **fp8_dispatch_grad** | **586.8 (3)** | **+3.0%** | **198.5 (2)** | **+5.9%** | **132.1 (2)** | **+5.7%** |
| dense row-wise (no transport) | | −5.6%* | | −1.9%* | | |
| experts row-wise (no transport) | | −3.6%* | | | | |
| all row-wise (no transport) | | −8.4%* | | −7.5%* | | |
| dense row-wise + dgrad | – | | 191.5 | +2.2% | 130.4 | +4.3% |
| experts row-wise + dgrad | – | | – | | 125.5 | +0.4% |
| all row-wise + dgrad | – | | – | | 123.7 | −1.0% |
| dense tensor + dgrad | 570.0 | 0.0% | 194.7 | +3.9% | 132.3 | +5.8% |
| dense tensor-fwd + dgrad | 571.9 | +0.4% | 196.5 | +4.9% | 132.4 | +5.9% |
| dense tensor, global amax (reverted) | | | | | 129–131 | +3–4.6% |
| dense tensor + fused qkv/gate-up (reverted) | | | | | 130–131 | +4–4.5% |
\* single 40-step probes (short-probe baseline 574.7). Any dense/expert FP8 on top of dgrad is neutral (tensor-wise) or slower (row-wise).

## d512 loss (cw-us-east-02a, 2384 steps, data-matched)
| run | config | mid (1191) | final Paloma macro |
|---|---|---|---|
| [fasttrack-moe-d512](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/fasttrack-moe-d512) | baseline | 3.4588 | 3.1559 (4-seed mean 3.1592) |
| [fp8-d512-disp-v2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/fp8-d512-disp-v2) | fp8_dispatch | 3.4605 | 3.1552 |
| [fp8-d512-dgrad-v2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/fp8-d512-dgrad-v2) | fp8_dispatch_grad | 3.4595 | 3.1540 |
| [fp8-d512-dgrad-s1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/fp8-d512-dgrad-s1) | fp8_dispatch_grad, seed 1 | 3.4552 | 3.1612 |
| [fp8-d512-allmm-dgrad](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/fp8-d512-allmm-dgrad) | all matmuls row-wise + dispatch_grad | 3.4599 | 3.1577 |
All within ~1σ. (`fp8-d512-disp/-alldisp/-dgrad` without `-v2` crashed at eval from the bug above; `fp8-d1280-dgrad` was cancelled when parking.)

## Why FP8 matmuls didn't pay
- d512 GEMMs are memory-bound (K=256/512): even pre-quantized FP8 is only 1.07–1.13× (1.54×/1.67× on q/o at d1024/d1280).
- XLA's Triton path runs the batched expert GEMMs at ~0.92–1.01× in FP8 — no speedup.
- Quantization passes don't fuse in XLA: at d1280 tensor-wise FP8 saved ~80 ms/step of dense GEMM time but added ~80 ms of casts/reductions/weight quantization; `shard_map` blocks fusing the cast into the norm, and removing it adds a global amax all-reduce (−1%).
- Fused qkv/gate-up GEMMs added a ~57 ms/step backward concatenate; FP8 dgrad needs an amax pass over the gradient; per-assignment all-to-all quantization (~9× rows) costs more than it saves.

## What it would take (if revisited)
- modded-nanogpt-style fused kernels: per-tensor scales with the cast fused into the producing norm/activation kernel (next-step amax as a side output, i.e. delayed scaling with headroom), weights quantized once per step after the optimizer, scales inside the GEMM — Triton/CuTe kernels in JAX (e.g. QuACK `norm_act_mod` / `gemm_epilogue`) plus delayed-scale state in the train state.
- A real SM90 FP8 expert GEMM with row/column scales in the epilogue (QuACK `GemmSm90` supports FP8 k-major), ideally with SwiGLU fused — only pays at d1024+.
- Cheaper non-FP8 wins first: embedding-gradient scatter (~6% at d512), MoE argsorts, all-to-all skew.

Commits (`fast-track-fp8`, local): `7cddca944e` row-wise FP8 + FP8 dispatch · `4062ad5ccd` --seed · `e59fab8e51` MoeTransport · `28a1b4da1a` fp8_dispatch_grad · `69115b8443` dropless-eval fix · `fe867e6b0f` prune losing transports + docs · `5c966673e4` tensor-wise dense FP8 · `470070338c` keep per-shard tensor-wise.

comments.body:
🤖 **KMA (KDA + MLA/Inkling + AttnRes) d512 tuning — final (Track A quality: 7 batches / 74 runs; Track B identical-math speed).** Branch `fast-track-kma-tune` (local, on top of `684b4c31d2`).

## Headline
- **Quality:** best config **B = 3.1039 ± 0.0027 (5 seeds)** vs KMA reference 3.1138 ± 0.0029 (5 seeds; −0.0099, ~4σ) and the no-feature baseline 3.1592 (**−0.055**).
- **Speed (identical math):** KMA d512 **469.6 → 691.2 ex/s (+47%)**, MFU 6.72 → 9.89 — now faster than the no-feature baseline (~570 on the same cluster). Two opt-in extras reach 749.8 ex/s (+60%).
- Caveat for fair comparison: several speedups are generic (bucketed Newton–Schulz, CE vocab tile, fused MoE input projections, sort-based MoE ranks, gather-based expand backward) and would also speed up the baseline; the AttnRes SAVE backward and merged stacks are KMA-specific.

**B flags:**
```
--local-mixer kda --kda-dt-range 0.02,0.5 --kda-gate-opt adam --kda-beta-opt muonh --kda-beta-lr-mult 2 \
--mla --mla-q-latent-div 2 --inkling-relpos --rel-extent 4096 --no-qk-norm --qk-mult 1.6 \
--rel-r-proj-opt adam --rel-proj-opt adam \
--attn-res --attn-res-num-blocks 8 --attn-res-query-lr-scale 0.1 --opt-set beta2=0.98
```
(learnable AttnRes key norm = `--attn-res-frozen-key-norm` omitted). B per-seed finals: 3.1018 / 3.1056 / 3.1077 / 3.1033 / 3.1013. Noise: 5 KMA ref seeds span 3.1095–3.1168; same-seed replicates differ by up to 0.005 (non-deterministic reductions) → single-run gaps < ~0.006 are noise.

## Multi-seed means
| config | seeds | final mean | Δ vs KMA 3.1138 | ex/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KMA reference | 5 | 3.1138 | 0 | 458 old / ~630 fast build |
| COMBO: extent 2048 + qk_mult 1.3 + β2 0.99 + KDA dt 0.02–0.5 | 4 | 3.1096 | −0.004 | ~640 |
| A: COMBO + qk 1.6 + β2 0.98 + extent 4096 | 3 (+1 replicate) | 3.1068 | −0.007 | ~625 |
| **B: A + learnable key norm + KDA beta LR 2×** | **5** | **3.1039** | **−0.0099** | ~630 |
| split AttnRes q/kv queries | 2 | 3.1152 | +0.001 | −4% |
| split, kv first-half, KDA write gates from q | 2 | 3.1150 | +0.001 | −6% |
| Full AttnRes (every sublayer a source) | 2 | 3.1188 | +0.005 | ~same |
| learnable key norm alone | 2 | 3.1127 | −0.001 | – |
| β2 0.99 alone | 2 | 3.1105 | −0.003 | – |
| extent 2048 alone | 2 | 3.1116 | −0.002 | – |
| qk 1.3 alone | 2 | 3.1120 | −0.002 | – |
| dt 0.02–0.5 alone | 2 | 3.1124 | −0.001 | – |

## What mattered
- **KDA:** small help from dt 0.02–0.5 and beta LR 2× (MuonH, in combination). Neutral: gate rank 64/256, dt 0.01–1.0, dt 0.03–0.5. Worse: beta scale 2 (+0.010), dt 0.005 (+0.006), dt 0.05 (+0.007), qkvo LR 0.7× (+0.004).
- **MLA/Inkling:** qk_mult (QK-norm off) is the strongest knob (0.7 +0.006, 1.3 −0.002, 1.6 −0.005; 2.0 +0.008 alone, fine inside B). Inkling extent 2048/4096 slightly helps (global layers see 4096 context). Neutral: Inkling LR 2×. Worse: KV latent 256 (+0.009), full-rank Q (+0.010). rel_dim 32 hung at step 0 (cancelled, not investigated).
- **⚠️ MLA absorbability:** the MLA global layers still apply the fast_track **K ShortConv** (depthwise causal conv over time on k, after W_UK). k stays linear in the KV latents but each channel mixes 4 positions, so inference absorption would need one absorbed query per conv lag rather than a single W_UK absorption. Removing it (strict form, `--model-set sconv_sites=attn,mlp`) costs **+0.020**.
- **AttnRes:** one block per layer (N ≥ 6 at L=6) is best; N=3 +0.005; Full AttnRes +0.005 (2 seeds); query LR 0.1× confirmed (0.3× +0.011); learnable key norm ≈ neutral alone, kept in B. **Split q/kv queries** (both variants + q-gate ablation, 2 seeds each, and inside COMBO): no gain, 4–6% slower.
- **Global:** LR 0.8×/1.25× worse (+0.009); 0.9×/1.1× neutral inside COMBO. Adam β2 (heuristic 0.996): 0.99/0.98 better (−0.003), 0.95 inside B −0.004 (1 seed), 0.999 worse (+0.008).

## Track B — identical-math speedups (cw-rno2a, vs same-cluster refs)
| change | parity evidence | ex/s |
|---|---|---|
| AttnRes SAVE backward (keep residuals instead of per-layer recompute; d512 default; peak 11.6 → 33 GiB) | CPU grad parity < 1e-4; 400-step loss pair | 473.6 → 573.9 (+21%) |
| one parameter stack per mixer kind under AttnRes (4 → 2) | tests | → 604.2 (+5%) |
| bucketed Newton–Schulz (same-shape matrices across leaves in one batched call) | equal within bf16 rounding; optimizer cost now ~noise | → 650.6 (+8%) |
| CE vocab tile 4096 → 8192 | step-0 loss identical; trajectory in replicate spread | ~638 → 658 (+3%) |
| sort-based MoE receiver ranks; gather-based MoE expand backward; KDA chunk states saved at d512 | exact-output tests (bitwise-identical grads for KDA) | compute 169.8 → 160.5 ms/step |
| one GEMM for each MoE block's input projections (router, latent down, shared gate/up) + one for shared down-projections | CPU grad parity < 1e-5 rel | 648 → 692 |
| **final default build** | 400-step loss inside the original-vs-original envelope; step-0 loss matches to 1e-5 | **469.6 → 691.2 (+47%)**, MFU 6.72 → 9.89, peak 31.9 GiB |
| opt-in: f32 embedding-grad accumulation (`--model-set embed_grad_accumulation=float32`; changes rounding) | full B run 3.1010 (no loss cost) | 691 → 738 (+6.8%) |
| opt-in: XLA command buffers (`--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=FUSION`; off due to #5675 B200 hang) | full run completed | +1.5% |
| both opt-ins | | 749.8 (+60%), MFU 10.73 |
Tried, no gain, reverted: PGLE, exact argmax top-k, saved MoE expert activations, fused KDA q/k/v/gate projections, disabling the inline watch. Remaining ~185 ms/step: ~155 compute + ~19 exposed comm (MoE dispatch/combine/a2a/experts ~49 + a2a, KDA ~32, CE ~12, MLA ~13.5, router top_k 6.7, AttnRes mix ~6.7).

🤖 **KMA d512 round C — KDA fp32 params, KDA LR tuning, SWA-first layers** (single seed each; constraints: Inkling extent back to 1024, Adam β1/β2 at heuristic defaults, frozen AttnRes key norm, QK-norm off). Branch `fast-track-kma-tune` (`410156bf79`, `2812dcc1b4`).

**Reference B0** (KDA dt 0.02–0.5, gate Adam, β MuonH LR 2×; MLA dm, qk_mult 1.6, extent 1024; AttnRes N=8, frozen key norm, query LR 0.1×): seeds 3.1098 / 3.1129 / 3.1125 → **mean 3.1117** (σ≈0.0017), ≈660 ex/s; **−0.047 vs baseline 3.1592**.

| kt-c3-K2 | K1 + A_log 0.3× | 3.4177 | 3.1095 | −0.0022 | 659 |
| kt-c2-swa1 | layer 0 = SWA (MLA+Inkling, window 2048) | 3.4161 | 3.1167 | +0.0050 | 669 |
| kt-c2-swa2 | layers 0–1 = SWA (MLA+Inkling) | 3.4141 | 3.1182 | +0.0065 | 655 |
| kt-c2-swa1gqa | layer 0 = baseline GQA SWA (RoPE, QK-norm) | 3.4274 | 3.1271 | +0.0154 | 665 |

**Takeaways:** nothing beats B0 beyond noise and the single-run winners don't stack (K1 −0.004). KDA fp32 (decay/gate/beta) is free in throughput (probes 655–662 vs 647 same-cluster base) and matches K3 — worth adopting for fidelity, not measured loss. A_log wants ≤1× LR (10× worse); other KDA LR multipliers are flat. SWA-first layers are worse (more layers → worse; GQA+RoPE clearly worse, +0.015); KDA beats softmax SWA in the early local layers, with only ~1% throughput gain from SWA in full runs. New flags: split `kda_a_log` / `kda_dt_bias` optimizer groups (`--kda-a-log-opt/-lr-mult`, `--kda-dt-bias-opt/-lr-mult`), `--model-set kda_gate_precision={compute,decay_fp32,gate_fp32,gate_beta_fp32}`, `--model-set swa_first_n=1|2` (+ `swa_first_mixer`).
